In the prop firm industry, when the total funded accounts with a single company exceed $300k, or when a trader makes several thousand USD in profit, accounts may sometimes be terminated without any clear explanation. I have experienced this with FTMO, Top One Trader, The Trading Pit, Blueberry, For Traders, and Fintokei. Of course, I did not break any rules or engage in gambling-style trading.

At the moment, there are still firms that continue to pay me without any issues. I want to trust them, but there is no guarantee that this will continue in the future.

Right now, I am waiting for payouts from four firms: Alpha Capital Group, Funded Next, ATFunded, and Lark Funding. If I receive them successfully, I will share them publicly with evidence.

I hope this will be helpful when you choose a prop firm.

I basically keep sharing my real-time experiences regarding payments, issues, and how they are handled, but do you think there is also value in sharing past issues and how they were handled?

To be honest, I am worried about retaliation when writing about my experiences with companies that have handled situations like this. However, if sharing my experiences can help someone else, I am willing to share as much as I can.

For example, with The Trading Pit, I continued trading with lot sizes that they had explicitly confirmed in advance were acceptable (such as 1 lot of XAU/USD on a 100k account). I successfully passed the challenge and made a profit. However, they later claimed that I had taken excessive risk. They only made some of the payments and refunds, and then closed my accounts, including a total of 300k in funded accounts and 200k in challenge accounts.

This is simply my personal experience, and it does not necessarily mean that you will have the same experience.

However, when you look at the reviews on Prop Firm Match, 9 out of 36 reviews — 25% — are 1-star reviews. That is one of the highest proportions of negative reviews among prop firms.
